title: Check LINK–CORE handshake recovery over USB
purpose: Check that the real role workers discard temporary keys and can complete a fresh authenticated exchange after each failure.
prerequisites: The permanent-identity bench pass is recorded for this LINK and CORE.
Both registered boards are running the exact role images below and are connected in normal USB mode.
Supervise the recovery procedure. Each application generates its own temporary signing key in RAM.

steps.action: Select the registered device and its peer.
steps.expected: The LINK and CORE each have a matching development build.
evidence: The LINK and CORE each have a matching development build.

steps.expected: Workshop saves each device record before reading its USB identity.
evidence: Workshop saves each device record before reading its USB identity.

steps.action: Connect both boards in normal mode and start the recovery test.
steps.expected: Each endpoint matches its selected registry record, current build and pre-test identity proof.
evidence: Each endpoint matches its selected registry record, current build and pre-test identity proof.

steps.action: Exercise entropy refusal, cancellation with a borrowed frame, a late completion, key-slot exhaustion and a signing failure.
steps.expected: Each board cleans up and completes a fresh temporary-key handshake with its peer after each failure. Nine recovery exchanges confirm all eight flights. The board rejects a queued operation with controlled deadline expiry or loss of continuity and checks that the shared radio budget refuses two packet sizes while its elapsed bound is unknown. The minimum free worker and USB stacks are at least 2,048 bytes on each role.
evidence: Each board cleans up and completes a fresh temporary-key handshake with its peer after each failure. Nine recovery exchanges confirm all eight flights. The board rejects a queued operation with controlled deadline expiry or loss of continuity and checks that the shared radio budget refuses two packet sizes while its elapsed bound is unknown. The minimum free worker and USB stacks are at least 2,048 bytes on each role.

steps.expected: Review the per-role failures, successful retries, minimum free USB and worker stack, peak heap, and progress of the competing control-flash and radio-status reads.
evidence: Review the per-role failures, successful retries, minimum free USB and worker stack, peak heap, and progress of the competing control-flash and radio-status reads.

steps.expected: Each report reopens with matching device and build, the shared run, recovery evidence and the trace digest.
evidence: Each report reopens with matching device and build, the shared run, recovery evidence and the trace digest.

steps.expected: Workshop saves separate LINK and CORE reports for this recovery run.
evidence: Workshop saves separate LINK and CORE reports for this recovery run.

rules.pass: Both pinned boards passed every recovery case, confirmed all nine fresh exchanges, met the measured reserves, and have reviewed, reopened and exported reports.
rules.fail: An accepted stale callback, a retained key after retirement, an unconfirmed retry or an out-of-budget measurement prevents acceptance.
rules.blocked: Missing verified identity evidence, exact build or unambiguous USB target blocks the attempt.
rules.incomplete: Timeout, lost response, cancellation, logout or interruption remains explicit; retain partial evidence and link any retry.
rules.limits: This supervised USB procedure uses RAM-only test signing keys, a fixed diagnostic entropy refusal and a signing callback refusal. Permanent identities prove board identity before and after the run. Radio work reads status. Physical RF timing and phone pairing have separate tests.
